But dining with my friend Fred Clancy, of the Irish bar, at Greenwich, the Mulligan came up, "inthrojuiced" himself to Clancy as he said, claimed relationship with him on the side of Brian Boroo, and drawing his chair to our table, quickly became intimate with us.

arxiv-1501-04269.title: On the Tong-type identity and the mean square of the error term for an extended Selberg class
arxiv-1501-04269.creator: Xiaodong Cao, Yoshio Tanigawa, Wenguang Zhai
arxiv-1501-04269.description: Abstract In 1956, Tong established an asymptotic formula for the mean square of the error term in the summatory function of the Piltz divisor function d 3 ​ ( n ) . d_{3}(n). The aim of this paper is to generalize Tong’s method to a class of Dirichlet series that satisfy a functional equation.

arxiv-2010-07213.title: Data Readiness Report CCS: General and reference Evaluation CCS: Software and its engineering Documentation CCS: Human-centered computing Walkthrough evaluations
arxiv-2010-07213.creator: Shazia Afzal, Rajmohan C, Manish Kesarwani, Sameep Mehta, Hima Patel
arxiv-2010-07213.description: Abstract . Data exploration and quality analysis is an important yet tedious process in the AI pipeline. Current practices of data cleaning and data readiness assessment for machine learning tasks are mostly conducted in an arbitrary manner which limits their reuse and results in loss of productivity.

arxiv-2108-03871.title: TransForensics: Image Forgery Localization with Dense Self-Attention
arxiv-2108-03871.creator: Jing Hao, Zhixin Zhang, Shicai Yang, Di Xie, Shiliang Pu
arxiv-2108-03871.description: Abstract Nowadays advanced image editing tools and technical skills produce tampered images more realistically, which can easily evade image forensic systems and make authenticity verification of images more difficult. To tackle this challenging problem, we introduce TransForensics, a novel image forgery localization method inspired by Transformers.

arxiv-2109-10038.title: VPN: Video Provenance Network for Robust Content Attribution Conference: European Conference on Visual Media Production; December 6–7, 2021; London, United Kingdom European Conference on Visual Media Production (CVMP ’21), December 6–7, 2021, London, United Kingdom Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3485441.

arxiv-2109-10038.description: Abstract . We present VPN - a content attribution method for recovering provenance information from videos shared online. Platforms, and users, often transform video into different quality, codecs, sizes, shapes, etc. or slightly edit its content such as adding text or emoji, as they are redistributed online.

arxiv-2206-02176.creator: Antika Sinha 1
arxiv-2206-02176.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Antika Sinha 1. We build and analyze the network of hundred top cited nodes (research papers and books from Google Scholar; strength or citation of the nodes range from about 44000 up to 100) starting early 1980 to till last year.

arxiv-2302-10509.title: Exploring the Possibility of Interacting Quintessence Model as an Alternative to the Λ \Lambda CDM Model
arxiv-2302-10509.creator: Nandan Roy
arxiv-2302-10509.description: Abstract This study examines interacting quintessence dark energy models and their observational constraints for a general parameterization of the quintessence potential, which encompasses a broad range of popular potentials. Four different forms of interactions are considered. The analysis is done by expressing the system as a set of autonomous equations for each interaction.

arxiv-2310-15091.title: Digital quantum simulation of lattice fermion theories with local encoding
arxiv-2310-15091.creator: Marco Ballarin, Giovanni Cataldi, Giuseppe Magnifico, Daniel Jaschke, Marco Di Liberto, Ilaria Siloi, Simone Montangero, Pietro Silvi
arxiv-2310-15091.description: Abstract We numerically analyze the feasibility of a platform-neutral, general strategy to perform quantum simulations of fermionic lattice field theories under open boundary conditions. The digital quantum simulator requires solely one- and two-qubit gates and is scalable since integrating each Hamiltonian term requires a finite (non-scaling) cost.

arxiv-2407-13708.title: Are We Ready for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Digital Pathology?
arxiv-2407-13708.creator: Ji-Hun Oh, Kianoush Falahkheirkhah, Rohit Bhargava
arxiv-2407-13708.description: Abstract The detection of semantic and covariate out-of-distribution (OOD) examples is a critical yet overlooked challenge in digital pathology (DP). Recently, substantial insight and methods on OOD detection were presented by the ML community, but how do they fare in DP applications?

arxiv-2410-06724.title: Does small-scale turbulence matter for ice growth in mixed-phase clouds?
arxiv-2410-06724.creator: G. Sarnitsky, G. Sardina, G. Svensson, A. Pumir, F. Hoffmann, B. Mehlig
arxiv-2410-06724.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by G. Sarnitsky, G. Sardina, G. Svensson, A. Pumir, F. Hoffmann, B. Mehlig. Representing the glaciation of mixed-phase clouds in terms of the Wegener-Bergeron-Findeisen process is a challenge for many weather and climate models, which tend to overestimate this process because cloud dynamics and microphysics are not accurately represented. As turbulence is essential for the transport of water vapour from evaporating liquid droplets to ice crystals, we developed a statistical model using established closures to assess the role of small-scale turbulence.

arxiv-2506-16970.title: Large Deviation Principles for Abelian Monoids
arxiv-2506-16970.creator: Daniel Keliher, Sun Woo Park
arxiv-2506-16970.description: Abstract . Following work of Mehrdad and Zhu [ MZ16 ] and of Liu [ Liu04a , Liu04b ] , we prove a large deviation principle for a broad class of integer-valued additive functions defined over abelian monoids. As a corollary, we obtain a large deviation principle for a generalized form of the Erdős-Kac theorem due to Liu. 1.

arxiv-2601-16615.title: AuroraEdge-V-2B: A Faster And Stronger Edge Visual Large Language Model
arxiv-2601-16615.creator: Xiang Chen
arxiv-2601-16615.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Xiang Chen. Recently, due to the advancement of multimodal technology, people are attempting to use visual large language models (VLLMs) in industrial production. Many deep learning models (DLMs) deployed in the production environment are gradually being replaced by VLLMs. Compared with DLMs, VLLMs have some advantages in industrial applications: (1) Their strong generalization ability enables them to perform well across a wide range of tasks. (2) They are flexible and can deal with unfamiliar samples through context learning quickly.

britannica-1911-cinnamon.title: Cinnamon (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-cinnamon.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-cinnamon.description: Article 'Cinnamon' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 6), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. small evergreen tree belonging to the natural order Lauraceae, native to Ceylon. The leaves are large, ovate-oblong in shape, and the flowers, which are arranged in panicles, have a greenish colour and a rather disagreeable odour. Cinnamon has been known from remote antiquity, and it was so highly prized among ancient nations that it was regarded as a present fit for monarchs and other great potentates.

govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HooverJEdgarKen.creator: Unknown
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-HooverJEdgarKen.description: Newspaper article on 'The Chancellor Manuscript,' the new book intertwining real people and events with a fictional premise that J. Edgar Hoover withheld vital information about the Kennedy and King assassinations.

pmc-10523417.title: Real-time monitoring of infant theta power during naturalistic social experiences
pmc-10523417.creator: Elena Throm, Anna Gui, Rianne Haartsen, Pedro F. da Costa, Robert Leech, Emily J.H. Jones
pmc-10523417.description: Infant-directed speech and direct gaze are important social cues that shape infant’s attention to their parents. Traditional methods for probing their effect on infant attention involve a small number of pre-selected screen-based stimuli, which do not capture the complexity of real-world interactions.

pmc-10698506.title: Paralog dispensability shapes homozygous deletion patterns in tumor genomes
pmc-10698506.creator: Barbara De Kegel, Colm J Ryan
pmc-10698506.description: Genomic instability is a hallmark of cancer, resulting in tumor genomes having large numbers of genetic aberrations, including homozygous deletions of protein coding genes. That tumor cells remain viable in the presence of such gene loss suggests high robustness to genetic perturbation.

pmc-11300978.title: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in women of reproductive age: a systematic review of local formularies
pmc-11300978.creator: Elizabeth Lovegrove, Alice Maidwell-Smith, Beth Stuart, Miriam Santer
pmc-11300978.description: BackgroundDepression is the second most common chronic condition affecting women of reproductive age; 23.4% of women enter pregnancy with depression and use of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) in pregnancy is often necessary for maternal wellbeing. However, SSRI use during pregnancy can cause congenital malformations, postpartum haemorrhage (PPH), and persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN).

pmc-11519251.title: A radiomics-based interpretable machine learning model to predict the HER2 status in bladder cancer: a multicenter study
pmc-11519251.creator: Zongjie Wei, Xuesong Bai, Yingjie Xv, Shao-Hao Chen, Siwen Yin, Yang Li, Fajin Lv, Mingzhao Xiao, Yongpeng Xie
pmc-11519251.description: ObjectiveTo develop a computed tomography (CT) radiomics-based interpretable machine learning (ML) model to preoperatively predict human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) status in bladder cancer (BCa) with multicenter validation.MethodsIn this retrospective study, 207 patients with pathologically confirmed BCa were enrolled and divided into the training set (n = 154) and test set (n = 53).

pmc-12375065.title: Spatial distribution dataset of 30-m resolution cropland in agricultural regions, Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
pmc-12375065.creator: Xingsheng Xia, Shenghui Lv, Meijuan Liu, Meng Yan, Qiong Chen, Yaozhong Pan
pmc-12375065.description: This study developed a 30-m resolution annual cropland dataset spanning 1988–2024 to resolve the unstable data quality and high sample acquisition costs in mapping cropland distributions in two agricultural regions of the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau (QTP): the Hehuang Valley (HV) and middle basin of the Yarlung Zangbo River and its two tributaries (the Lhasa and Nianchu rivers; MBYZR and LNR, respectively).

pmc-12417055.title: Predictors of reintervention following hydrodistension as a treatment for adhesive capsulitis
pmc-12417055.creator: James Allen, Samir Asmar, James Vun, Adrian Andronic, Luke Budworth, Paul David Cowling, Yorkshire Upper Limb Collaborative
pmc-12417055.description: AimsThe primary outcome was to determine the proportion of patients with adhesive capsulitis who required reintervention following a treatment of hydrodistension. The secondary outcome was to identify predictors of reintervention.MethodsA total of 712 hydrodistension procedures from six NHS trusts were included for statistical analysis. Minimum follow-up was 18 months. The primary outcome was the reintervention rate.

pmc-13201770.title: Liver transcriptome dynamics in Holstein cows during the periparturient transition
pmc-13201770.creator: Nayan Bhowmik, Mariana da Silva, Alejandro Castaneda, Asha M Miles, Congjun Li, Curtis P Van Tassell, Ransom L Baldwin, J Eduardo Rico, George E Liu
pmc-13201770.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). During the periparturient phase, dairy cows undergo profound physiological, metabolic, and immunological changes that affect their health, productivity, and reproductive efficiency, with the liver playing a central role in adaptation. In this study, liver transcriptomic changes were assessed in six multiparous Holstein cows by targeting samples approximately 21 d before expected calving date (D-21) and 7 d after calving (D+7) using RNA sequencing.

pmc-13474031.title: Controllable Cascade Aggregation Ion Programmed Nanomachines and Simple Isolation Enable Tumor‐Derived Small Extracellular Vesicles Detection for Enhanced Breast Cancer Assessment
pmc-13474031.creator: Zhihao Zhang, Zijing Liu, Xiangyue Meng, Pengjun Jiang, Jie Qu, Yu Jiang, Binxu Qiu, Jie Chen, Piaopiao Chen
pmc-13474031.description: Small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) carry biomolecules that reflect their cellular origin, making them attractive biomarkers for breast cancer assessment and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)‐status discrimination. However, existing methods involve lengthy isolation procedures and exhibit poor detection performance due to severe interference from excessive impurities.

pmc-13508084.title: Organocatalytic Asymmetric Formal Aza-[3 + 2] Cycloaddition via Domino Michael/Acetalization: Stereoselective Access to 3,4-cis-Disubstituted Pyrrolidines and Pot-Economical Total Syntheses of (−)-Kainic Acid and (−)-Domoic Acid
pmc-13508084.creator: Yutaro Hatano, Hinata Odaira, Toshiki Tachibana, Yujiro Hayashi
pmc-13508084.description: An asymmetric catalytic formal aza-[3 + 2] cycloaddition (domino Michael/acetalization reaction) between aldehydes and benzyl N-(3-nitro-2-propen-1-yl)­carbamate catalyzed by a diphenylprolinol silyl ether has been developed, affording 3,4-cis-disubstituted pyrrolidines with excellent diastereo- and enantioselectivity. The transformation proceeds via a domino sequence comprising a Michael addition followed by hemiacetalization.

pmc-13671258.title: Liquid Chromatography Coupled With High‐Resolution Mass Spectrometry Profiling of Metabolites in Cassia alata Flower Extracts and Their DPPH Free Radical Scavenging Activity
pmc-13671258.creator: Adonai Yin‐Anaab Kunduzore, Shakira Ibrahim, Auphedeous Yinme Dang‐i, Michael Adu‐Frimpong, Salma Elshamy, Nikolai Kuhnert, James Ziemah
pmc-13671258.description: Cassia alata flowers remain phytochemically under‐characterized relative to the leaves. However, floral tissues can harbour distinct and, in some species, more abundant phenolic and flavonoid profiles, representing an unexploited source of antioxidant phytochemicals with potential functional‐food and nutraceutical relevance. Also, Cassia alata L.
